## TL;DR

The release-update dialog now teaches users how to upgrade instead of only
linking to the GitHub release. `GET /api/release/available` returns two new
fields — `installKind` and `upgradeCommand` — computed by a new exported helper
`upgradeInstruction()` in `src/commands/upgrade.ts`, the *same* detection
`repoos upgrade` uses. The dialog renders the command in a code block with a
Copy button (shared `copyToClipboard`, so it works on insecure origins),
relabels the old "Upgrade" link to "Release notes", and adds a truthful note
that the command runs in a terminal and an already-running server keeps the old
version until restarted. Dismissal is remembered per version in `localStorage`,
so the banner stays gone across page loads.

## Work and rationale

The core decision was one function as the single source of truth for both the
CLI and the server. `upgradeInstruction({ installRoot, version, channel })`
mirrors `cmdUpgrade`'s detection order exactly: (1) a recognized package-manager
path wins; (2) a missing `.build-info.json` (no version) means a source
checkout; (3) otherwise a standalone/curl install, with `--channel <name>` when
the installed version carries a prerelease identifier. `cmdUpgrade` now calls
the same function, so CLI output and dialog text cannot drift.

Two smaller pure helpers: `channelFromVersion()` reads the channel from the
installed semver (`0.6.0-beta.1` → `beta`) — the only per-install signal that
exists, since there is no stored channel config; and `SOURCE_UPGRADE_COMMAND`
centralizes the source-checkout text. The spec asked for
`git pull && bun install && bun run build`; the CLI previously printed
`git pull && bun run build`, so I updated the CLI and the one doc quoting it.

On the server, `getAvailableRelease` gained an `installInfo()` helper that
spreads `installKind` / `upgradeCommand` into both the success payload and the
offline *fallback* (what the dialog gets when the update check times out).

The dialog stays within the existing styled-component conventions: lucide
`Copy`/`Check` icons and the shared `Button`, no native tooltips or `title`. The
code block uses theme tokens (`--bg-2`, `--border`, `--txt`) so the
hard-coded-color guard and rendered contrast audit stay green. Copy delegates to
`copyToClipboard` rather than `navigator.clipboard`, because RepoOS is often
served over plain-HTTP LAN or Tailscale addresses where the async clipboard API
is undefined; the helper falls back to `execCommand` and reports success so a
blocked copy does not falsely claim "Copied".

For dismissal I keyed on the *available version* rather than a boolean: the
banner re-appears only when `latestVersion` differs from the dismissed version,
so a newer release still surfaces. Every `localStorage` access is in try/catch.

For the declared shots I added one preview fixture, `release:updateAvailable`,
that pins the dialog open with a synthetic "newer release available" payload —
the live preview board usually reports `available: false`, so the command block
would never render without it. It is registered in `SHOT_PREVIEW_FIXTURE_IDS`,
mapped to the `dialog` capture container, and listed in `docs/previews.md`.

Tests: `releases.test.ts` covers `upgradeInstruction` across the four named
cases plus `channelFromVersion`, the dialog component (code text, relabelled
link + href, fake-clipboard copy, localStorage dismissal), and the capture-race
regression below.

## Approaches tried

A UI-only implementation that re-derived the install kind client-side was
rejected: the browser cannot see the install path, and the scope boundary with
#1072 requires a plain exported server-side helper. I considered reading the
channel from a config key, but none exists.

## Challenges and blockers

The main subtlety was reconciling command text: the spec demanded `bun install`
and that the text match the CLI. Updating the CLI (and the one doc that quoted
it) satisfied both — a source checkout that changed dependencies needs it.

The fixture had a capture race the server's UI verification caught twice, even
though the marker *was* applied and the component tests passed. A capture mounts
`ReleaseUpdateNotification` *before* App's `repo.init()` loads `/api/health`
(children mount first), so the live `/api/release/available` fetch lands first
with `available: false`; the original health `watch` only re-applied the fixture
while `release.value` was empty, so once the real payload won the fixture never
applied. The durable fix makes the fixture a **reactive module pin**:
`applyShotPreviewFixture` seeds `pinnedAvailableRelease` (a Vue `ref`) and the
component opens the dialog from a `watch` on it, so "marker set" and "dialog
open" happen together with no dependence on health timing. A second re-run
failed *earlier* — the marker itself was missing, since the App's fixture pass
is gated on `/api/health` reporting a preview build and a capture can settle
before `repo.init()` resolves. I added a `watch` on `repo.health?.isPreviewBuild`
in `App.vue` that re-applies the URL fixture the moment health arrives, fixing
this for every declared state. After that the declared shots captured cleanly.

This session resumed the work after a crash-recovery handoff, so most of the
implementation was already on the branch. The branch had drifted behind `main`;
merging it was conflict-free and collapsed the scoped diff back to this task's
own files. The last repeated handoff failure was not code: the report draft ran
over the 1,200-word limit, so I trimmed it below the cap. The board kept
restarting the engineer on that same message because it replayed from the stored
task frontmatter, not from fresh code.

One residual test-hygiene fix: the fixture regression test now removes the
applied-state attribute in its `finally`, so a later test cannot observe a stale
marker left by the fixture mount.

## Key learnings

- `repoos upgrade` has no channel config to read — the channel lives in the
  installed version string, so detection must parse the semver prerelease tag.
- The offline fallback payload of `/api/release/available` is a real render path;
  any new field must be filled there too, not just on success.
- A preview capture can outrun both `/api/health` and the App's fixture pass, so
  a component-local fixture gated on `isPreviewBuild` is racy when the capture
  also triggers a competing live fetch. Prefer a **reactive module pin** set by
  `applyShotPreviewFixture` — the same pattern `pinnedIntegration` /
  `pinnedRemoteStatus` already use.
- Mocking `fetch` with `mockResolvedValue(new Response(...))` is a trap when a
  test mounts the component more than once; the body is spent after one read.
